title: trimprompt (npm) installs shell shims into Cursor/Claude Code command paths and ships fully obfuscated modules that pair child_process with outbound host reporting
summary: trimprompt markets itself as a token-saving proxy for AI coding agents, but nearly every runtime module (cache-manager.js, ccr.js, executor.js, file-watcher.js, hooks/claude-hook.js, mcp.js, proxy-conv.js, proxy-resp.js, sync.js, tracker.js, all filters/*.js) is hex-mangled `_0x...` obfuscated JavaScript. Verified by unpacking the latest tarball (1.0.49): postinstall.js auto-runs `node cli.js shims install` and tells the user to restart Cursor/Claude Code so the shims intercept agent command output; shims.js spawns powershell/pwsh via execSync; and the obfuscated sync.js and tracker.js combine child_process with HTTP POSTs carrying hostname/identifier fields — the shape of host reconnaissance and beaconing, with destinations hidden behind the string-array obfuscation. Pervasive obfuscation plus install-time execution in the agent command path is inconsistent with a legitimate prompt-trimming utility. Flagged as malware by OSV (MAL-2026-13462). Recorded as high rather than critical because the exfiltration destinations and a remote-command channel could not be recovered from the obfuscated code.
